differences.text: Button avatars are opted into with `interactive` because an element cannot see click listeners (upstream's onClick element swap). href still wins over interactive.

The role and name live on the inner root element (role=img, or the link/button), not on the host, so the name can sit next to its tooltip description in one tree. A host aria-label overrides the derived name and is followed; a host aria-hidden hides the whole avatar natively.

The fallback surface is the Tecton avatar fill and ink (--tecton-color-avatar-fill / -text) instead of --color-neutral / --color-text-secondary. The Tecton design specifies 40/32/24/18px avatars and accent colours per instance; neither is a Tecton decision for this library (tecton-theme.md 6, 11), so the Astryx size scale stays.
Image URLs (src, fallback-src) go through the resource URL policy (safeUrl): script schemes and data: URLs are refused and the initials show. Upstream loads any string.

core.avatar.notes: Guides: [mwg:accessible-web-components] name and role inside the shadow root, delegatesFocus; [mwg:styling-web-components] parts and private custom properties; [mwg:shadow-dom] slots; [mwg:security] URL policy; [mwg:contrast-color] no user-supplied colours exist upstream, so the fixed Tecton pair is used.

api.notes: Drawn at medium and large avatar sizes; replaces the built-in shape glyph.

differences.text: The label reaches the avatar through avatarContext.reportStatusLabel (a context call from the dot), not a ref written in the commit phase; it works at any depth in the status slot and needs no introspection of a `label` prop.

Success and error plates are the Tecton status main roles (--tecton-color-status-success / -error) with the surface colour as ink, matching tecton-astryx's avatar status dot override; plate and ink keep at least 3:1 in both modes (tested).
Forced colours draw each shape explicitly (solid disc, hollow ring, disc with a bar) with system colours instead of losing the plate.

differences.text: The group name is the host aria-label (default "Avatars", localised) and follows attribute changes; the keyboard hint and any author aria-describedby are combined into one description (element references, or text on Tier 2) because ids cannot cross the shadow root.

Roving items are the members whose `control` is not null (interactive avatars and overflow); members tell the group when they become interactive through avatarGroupContext.refresh(), instead of upstream's post-commit DOM query for [data-avatar-item].
